messages:
customer-jdoe: Hey team — our web app started showing very slow streaming responses around 15:10 UTC. TTFB is fine for non-stream (sync) calls but streaming p95/p99 looks awful. User-visible lag: first chunk arrives ~2s later than usual, then chunks come fast. This started after yesterday's runtime rollout. Can you triage?

support-bot: Thanks for the report <@customer-jdoe>. I've filed INC-1841 and routed to support. Can you confirm region, model and whether you were using `stream=true`?

customer-jdoe: region=us-west-2, model=redwood/text-3b, yes `stream=true`. Non-stream `stream=false` calls return in ~250ms total, streaming has TTFB ~2.3s, total time ~2.7s. Used same key across tests.

liz: thanks, grabbing logs. Do you have a repro curl? if not, I'll run an internal repro with your workload.

customer-jdoe: here's a quick repro we used:
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true" \\\n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" \\\n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\n -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":120}'
```
I can drop a HAR if needed.

devon: FYI infra alert fired at 15:12 UTC: ops-bot message below.

ops-bot: ALERT: streaming-worker-p99 latency increased from 180ms -> 2.1s in us-west-2 (15:10 UTC). Trigger: p99 threshold breached.

liz: I reproduced locally against a staging cluster using the same model and got similar behaviour. Noticed that with `stream=true` the first chunk flush was delayed until ~2s; subsequent chunks were fine and small. Non-stream path uses the same model but returns in one shot ~200ms.

prakash: possible networking/proxy change? We rolled out proxy v2 last night in us-west-2 that changed `proxy_buffering` defaults. If proxy buffers until a certain amount or timeout, it could delay first chunk. Checking deploy logs.

prakash: confirmed — nginx-proxy v2.1.0 was rolled 02:30 UTC with default `proxy_buffering on` and `proxy_send_timeout 60s`. Previous config had `proxy_buffering off` for streaming routes.

sara: observability notes: per-route traces show the runtime emitted first chunk at 120ms, then nothing forwarded to customer until ~2.1s. So runtime->proxy flush seems absent. Runtime logs:
```
[2026-03-14T15:10:12Z] model=text-3b request_id=xyz first_chunk_emitted=true emitted_at_ms=120
[2026-03-14T15:10:12Z] proxy_forward_delay=2000ms route=/v1/generate stream=true
```
This indicates the runtime produced data quickly but some layer buffered it.

liz: that matches the hypothesis. @prakash can you confirm if the proxy treats `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` differently after the upgrade?

prakash: digging. The new proxy image turns on `proxy_buffering` for all upstreams unless you opt-out per location block. We missed adding `proxy_buffering off` for streaming endpoints in the new template.

devon: ok, remediation path: add `proxy_buffering off` back to streaming location blocks and roll hotfix to us-west-2. Also consider setting `proxy_busy_buffers_size` and `proxy_buffer_size` more conservative so small chunks stream.

liz: timeline for hotfix?

prakash: I can cut a config hotpatch in 10m and reload nginx with zero-downtime. Will push to prod canary then full us-west-2 if green.

support-bot: Progress note: hotpatch scheduled. We informed customer about potential workaround: use non-streaming calls or route to us-east-1 while we patch.

customer-jdoe: thanks — non-streaming is an awkward fallback for us because we need partial tokens for progressive UI. Can you ETA the fix?

prakash: canary in 15m, full in ~40m assuming no regressions. I'll post updates here.

sara: added a temporary dashboard tile to show `first_chunk_forward_latency` per region so we can monitor rollback impact. Also flagged potential impact on other models (text-1b, text-3b).

liz: mitigation notes for customers: 1) temporary route to other region, 2) short-term client workaround: set smaller `max_tokens` or use shorter prompts to force the runtime to emit earlier? (not ideal), 3) server-side: patch proxy to `proxy_buffering off` for streaming endpoints.

devon: long-term: we should add CI check to nginx template that validates streaming locations keep buffering off. Also add an integration test that asserts first_chunk_forward_latency < 500ms for a synthetic streaming request. Filing infra task.

prakash: hotpatch applied to canary at 15:28 UTC. Monitoring.

ops-bot: NOTICE: canary metrics show p99 decreased from 2.1s -> 240ms in canary.

prakash: promoting to full rollout now.

ops-bot: NOTICE: us-west-2 streaming-worker-p99 back to 230ms (15:41 UTC).

liz: closing loop with customer: <@customer-jdoe> we pushed a config hotfix to stop buffering for streaming routes in us-west-2. Can you re-test and confirm?

customer-jdoe: re-tested at 15:45 UTC — streaming TTFB back to ~210ms. Huge improvement, thanks everyone. We'll keep an eye for edge cases.

liz: follow-ups: 1) postmortem to document how proxy template change slipped through, 2) infra CI + integration test for streaming TTFB, 3) runbook update for support to check `proxy_buffering` when investigating streaming regressions, 4) customer follow-up email with RCA and mitigation credit. I'll own the support runbook item.

devon: adding runtime config option to emit a small preface chunk immediately for streaming (0-1 token) as extra protection vs buffering. This would make TTFB observable even if someone accidentally enables buffering. Filing ENG-4276.

sara: I'll attach traces and logs to INC-1841 and the postmortem doc.

support-bot: Incident INC-1841 resolved and linked to postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-1841 (draft).

customer-jdoe: thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

liz: nice teamwork. Marking this thread resolved but keeping postmortem in progress.
